subject.storage: std::vector<std::byte> buffer; explicit PipelineSlot(std::size_t cap) : buffer(cap) {}
subject.construction: value-initialization: one heap allocation of cap bytes followed by eager zero-initialization of all cap bytes (touches every page)
subject.site_kind: per-slot owned I/O staging buffer (read fills, write drains)

lifecycle_steps.code: apps/sluice-copy/main.cpp + cli_parse.cpp; caller opens src/dst fds

run_pipelined_copy_with_backend pre-checks: buffer_size/pipeline_depth/workers nonzero; kMaxBufferSize=64MiB; kMaxPipelineDepth=64; kMaxPipelineBytes=512MiB; product overflow; rejects invalid_state BEFORE any allocation
lifecycle_steps.notes: capacity is caller-owned and validated up front

ONE vector allocation + eager zero-init per slot, ONCE per copy operation, BEFORE the Runtime is built/started; bad_alloc translated to IoError::no_space; slots.reserve(depth) is the only growth (pointer vector)

lifecycle_steps.code: run_task_to_result<CopyStats> builds/starts ApplicationRuntime + caller backend (CLI: ThreadPoolBackend)
lifecycle_steps.notes: no buffer involvement; backend workers_ reserve is setup-only

lifecycle_steps.code: Phase 1 submit window: up to pipeline_depth submit_read at chunk_offset = i*buffer_size; ThreadPoolBackend pread into buffer.data()+filled
lifecycle_steps.notes: kernel overwrites [0,N) for full chunks; pages already resident from eager init; EOF tail chunk overwrites only [0,filled) — bytes [filled,N) keep zero-init but are never read by the write side

lifecycle_steps.code: after await_slot_write: ws->chunk_offset += buffer_size*pipeline_depth; filled=0; written=0; state=idle; submit_slot_read reuses SAME buffer
lifecycle_steps.notes: no realloc, no re-init, no memset; buffer address stable for whole operation (L7); reuse count per slot = number of chunk cycles ~= ceil(file_bytes/(buffer_size*pipeline_depth))

lifecycle_steps.code: Phase 3 drain (error path) / Phase 4 sync_data/sync_all (clean path)
slots vector destructs (task object end) -> each vector frees its block; one free per slot per copy operation

q1_vector_allocation_per_op_or_setup_onl.evidence: copy_task.cpp:446-456 constructs all slots once before run_task_to_result; no allocation in the Phase 1/2 loops

q2_slot_reuse_count.answer: unbounded within one copy operation: each slot is reused for chunk cycle after chunk cycle until EOF; reuse count per slot ~= ceil(file_bytes/(buffer_size*pipeline_depth)) (e.g. 1 GiB file, 1 MiB x depth 8 -> 128 reuses per slot)

q3_buffer_fully_overwritten_by_read.answer: yes for full chunks (pread fills [0,buffer_size), overwriting every zero-initialized byte); EOF tail chunk overwrites only [0,filled)
q3_buffer_fully_overwritten_by_read.evidence: submit_slot_read reads [chunk_offset+filled, +buffer_size-filled) into buffer.data()+filled; await_read_fill retries short reads to full-or-EOF

q4_short_read_partial_valid_length.answer: yes: filled tracks valid bytes; short reads retry within slot; EOF tail is a partial valid length; write side only drains [0,filled)

q5_slot_count_determined_by.answer: pipeline_depth caller parameter (CLI default 1 = Version A sequential; caps kMaxPipelineDepth=64, kMaxPipelineBytes=512MiB total)

q6_capacity_equals_active_inflight_depth.answer: yes: in steady state all pipeline_depth slots have reads outstanding (read overlap); writes are single-outstanding by design; buffer capacity == logical in-flight read depth
q6_capacity_equals_active_inflight_depth.evidence: copy_task.cpp Phase 1 pre-submit window + Phase 2 round-robin

q7_resize_or_growth.answer: none: per-slot buffer size fixed at construction; the slots pointer-vector is reserve(depth)+push_back (no reallocation); no resize/reserve on buffers

q8_production_steady_state_heap_allocati.answer: no per-op heap allocation in the copy steady state: buffers pre-built, Completions address-stable; ThreadPoolBackend uses fixed persistent workers with bounded dispatch storage (setup-time reserve only)
q8_production_steady_state_heap_allocati.status: CODE FACT (task side) + CODE FACT (backend construction side); steady-state dynamic-allocation absence is CODE FACT by inspection, not yet by measurement
q8_production_steady_state_heap_allocati.evidence: copy_task.cpp steady-state loops; src/async/threadpool_backend.cpp workers_.reserve at construction; bounded dispatch ring per ADR threadpool contract
